full_judgment:
2. Facts giving rise to the present appeal are that the appellant as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous Case (Pre-emption) No.28 of 1995 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Natore, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the land transferred by registered, kabala dated 27-2-1995 in favour of pre-emptee respondent Nos. 1-4. The miscellaneous case was allowed ex- parte by order dated 3-3-1997. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein who were pre-emptee opposite-parties Nos.2 and 4 in the miscellaneous case filed, an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for setting aside the ex- parte order allowing the pre-emption application stating, inter alia, that the summonses of the miscellaneous case were not served upon them; they came to know about the ex-parte order for the first time on 26-5-1997 when the pre-emptor disclosed that he got the case land through preemption; then the petitioners enquired in to the matter by engaging a lawyer and came to know definitely about the ex-parte order on 29-5-1997; the petitioners were seriously prejudiced by the ex-parte order allowing the pre-emption application and hence filed the application for setting the said order. 

 4. The pre-emptor-opposite party, appellant herein contested the said application by filing a written objection contending, inter alia, that the pre-emptee-petitioners received the summonses of the pre-emption case from the process server on 16-6-1995 by putting their left thumb impression; the summonses of the pre-emption case were also served upon the pre-emptee-petitioners through registered post; on 8-8-1996 the pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 through his lawyer prayed for time on behalf of all the pre-emptee-opposite parties for filing written objection and the Court allowed the prayer; subsequently as the pre-emptee-opposite parties did not file any written objection, the case was allowed ex-parte. The pre-emptor filed application before the court for getting delivery of possession of the case land through Court. The prayer was allowed and on 26-5-1997 the process server of the Court delivered possession of the case land to him and on 24-7-1997 the pre-emption miscellaneous case was finally disposed of on full satisfaction. The pre-emptee-petitioners filed the application for setting aside the ex-parte order by making false statements only to harass the pre-emptor and, as such, the same was liable to be rejected. 

 14. We find nothing wrong with the view taken by the learned Judge of the single Bench in view of the evidence on record. In this regard, we restate the law that in case of allegation of non-service of summons upon the defendant/opposite party, as the case may be, the onus is upon the plaintiff/petitioner that the summons of the suit or the case was served upon the defendant/opposite patty. 

 15. From the leave granting order, it appears that submission was made to the effect that when the summonses of the pre-emption miscellaneous case were served upon the pre-emptee-petitioners their father Yeazuddin was present but they did not "produce their father Yeazuddin" presumably for examination as a witness to deny the fact of service of summonses upon them, but on perusal of the evidence of the OPWs, it appears that none of them made any such statement, even no suggestion was given to PW1 that his father Yeazuddin was present when the process server served summons upon him. Therefore, we do not find any merit on the said submission. We also hold that in case of allegation of non-service of summons upon the defendant/opposite party, as the case may be, the second clause of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code "or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing" shall not be attracted, so we find no merit on the other submissions of the learned Advocate-on-record for the pre-emptor-appellant as well as noted in the leave granting order.
